newsitem.title: BELGIUM: STINNES JOINT VENTURE OUTSIDE EU MERGER LAW.
newsitem.headline: STINNES JOINT VENTURE OUTSIDE EU MERGER LAW.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday plans by Germany's Stinnes AG and Haniel to form a joint venture for waterway transports in Belgium did not fall within the scope of the EU's merger regulation.
Instead, the European Union executive said the deal would be reviewed under other EU competition rules.

Under the merger regulation, the Commission must complete a routine investigation within one month. However, if a deal is reviewed under other EU treaty rules, there is no fixed deadline. Because of this, companies often prefer that their joint ventures are reviewed under the merger regulation.

The proposal by Stinnes AG's RS Partnership and Haniel Reederei Holding GmbH to share control of Belgian shipping company De Grave NV was notified to the Commission for clearance under the merger regulation on July 9.

But the Commission said that besides this joint venture both parent companies would continue to be active in the watership transport business in other member states, especially in the Netherlands, Germany and France.
Both parent companies would retain significant activities in the same markets as their joint venture, it said.

"Since this finding seems likely to give rise to coordination of the competitive behaviour of the parent companies amongst themselves or between them and the joint venture the Commission decided that the proposed operation does not constitute a concentration under the merger regulation."
"The agreement now falls to be examined under other applicable competition rules," it added.
